content: Action, based in Wilmington, Massachusetts, provides ambulance services for both emergency situations and patient transfers. They deliver emergency and non-emergency pre-hospital medical care and transportation for individuals who are ill or injured. Currently, Action is contracted to serve as the emergency medical services (EMS) provider for various communities located north of Boston through 2008. Their ambulances are equipped with GPS technology, which allows them to identify and dispatch the closest and most appropriate ambulance to respond to emergencies. This GPS system also facilitates their regular collaborations with Boston MedFlight. Action was founded in 1977 by Dr. Harry Portman and his two sons, Stan and David, with an initial fleet of two ambulances. As their fleet expanded, they established a new operational base in Lynn, Massachusetts. Currently, Action's headquarters are located in Wilmington, Massachusetts. Action provides primary advanced life support (ALS) ambulance services to several towns, including Melrose, Nahant, North Reading, Swampscott, Wakefield, Wilmington, and Woburn, among others. They also offer backup ALS coverage to Lexington and Winchester. In their newest contract, they provide both ALS and basic life support (BLS) response services to the town of Ipswich. In January 2005, Action approached Northern Essex Community College (NECC) to address the need for an EMT training program in the Merrimack Valley area. They worked closely with NECC during the planning and design phases of the program. NECC's governance approval process was completed in November 2005, and the program received approval from the NECC Board of Trustees on April 5, 2006. The college subsequently submitted an application for accreditation to the Massachusetts Office of Emergency Medical Services (OEMS). Following an on-site visit on January 17, 2006, the program received full approval from the Massachusetts OEMS. The paramedic technology program prepares students for careers in pre-hospital emergency medical care. Graduates of the program are eligible for certification by the Massachusetts OEMS, allowing them to practice within the state. Additionally, they are qualified to take the National Registry of Emergency Medical Technicians-Paramedic (NREMT-P) examination. In June 2007, Action collaborated with the city of Woburn, Massachusetts, to help it achieve the designation of Heart Safe Community from the Massachusetts Office of Emergency Health Services. This effort involved working with the mayor's office and the fire department. The Heart Safe Community program, developed by the Massachusetts OEMS in conjunction with the Department of Public Health and the American Heart Association, aims to improve survival rates for individuals experiencing sudden cardiac arrest. Communities earn this designation by completing community CPR training, equipping emergency response vehicles with automated external defibrillators (AEDs), and placing AEDs in public locations where large groups of people gather or where individuals are at higher risk for cardiac arrest. Action also engages in public safety initiatives, such as participating in mock prom crash demonstrations to raise awareness, teaching CPR classes, and organizing annual blood drives.
